Generated by `junction principal --app api/src/app.ts --services api/src/services`. **Do not edit.**

Who a caller **arrives as**, and who they **become** before the Data boundary.

`db/access.snapshot.md` is the other half and it commits the predicate —
`workspaceId != auth().workspaceId`. This commits the predicate's **input**.
A resolver that emits the wrong tenant changes no line of that file, so
without this one the whole API half of tenancy has no diffable face.

No values anywhere below. A claim's NAME is a fact about the application; a
claim's VALUE is a caller.

## Tenancy

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Strategy | `row` |
| Column | `workspaceId` |
| Claim on the principal | `workspaceId` |
| A request names its tenant by | the X-Workspace-Id header or ?workspace_id= |

Under `strategy row` the tenant is a value on the principal, so **the claim is
the whole mechanism** — a caller holding none reads nothing, with a 200.

## Resolver — `createApp({ principal })`

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Kind | `membership` |
| Function | `membershipClaim` |
| Membership proved by | `workspaceMember` |
| Caller column | `userId` |
| Tenant column | `workspaceId` |
| Standing column | `role` |
| Capability grants | `capabilities` |
| Read alongside | `workspace` |

**No row is no claim.** A caller naming a tenant they do not belong to comes out
holding nothing — an empty screen and a gate that grades them a stranger — rather
than a full principal belonging to somebody else. That is the one line the whole
arrangement rests on.

## Claims

What this resolver may merge onto the principal, by name.

| Claim | |
| --- | --- |
| `workspaceId` | the tenant — read by the desugared `@@deny` on every scoped model |
| `memberRole` | a standing, graded by the app's own `getLevel` |
| `capabilities` | the grant set — read by the Data boundary's capability grid (`FJS-D151`), which is the one claim name this framework fixes rather than the app |

`userId` and `id` are refused by name: a claim says what a caller HOLDS for this
request, never who they are. Identity is `IAuth`'s and nothing else's.

## Standing

Read from `WorkspaceMember.role`, carried as `memberRole`.

| Declared value |
| --- |
| `viewer` |
| `billing` |
| `developer` |
| `admin` |
| `owner` |

5 value(s).

**The value→level mapping is not here and is not derivable.** `getLevel` is a
function the app hands to `GatePlugin`, and a client answers plugin names rather
than instances. What this file can grade is the SET: a value added to the ladder
and not to `getLevel` is a caller silently graded at whatever the default answers,
and the enum gaining a member is the visible edge of that. The mapping itself is
executed by litestone's `verifyGateLadder`.

## What the tenant rules reach

| | Count | Models |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Scoped by column | 18 | `Invitation` · `Secret` · `ApiKey` · `Server` · `Network` · `Project` · `Environment` · `App` · `Domain` · `Deployment` · `Job` · `Recipe` · `FeatureFlag` · `NotificationChannel` · `AlertRule` · `Dashboard` · `AuditEvent` · `RegistryImage` |
| Scoped by delegation | 14 | `ServerEvent` · `Volume` · `ServerNetwork` · `AppServer` · `AppNetwork` · `DeploymentStep` · `JobRun` · `RecipeRun` · `DiskUsage` · `CleanupRun` · `FlagOverride` · `AlertRuleChannel` · `AlertEvent` · `DashboardWidget` |
| Exempt — `@@tenant(none)` | 14 | `Credential` · `Session` · `Verification` · `OauthFlow` · `User` · `Account` · `Workspace` · `WorkspaceMember` · `OutpostNonce` · `Blueprint` · `BlueprintParam` · `Backup` · `HubConfig` · `NotificationPreference` |

An exemption is a decision, so it is listed by name rather than counted. A model
moving into this row is a model every tenant can now read.

Whether these rules HOLD is a separate question with an executed answer —
litestone's `verifyTenantIsolation()`, which seeds a row for one tenant and has
another try to reach it.

## Refusals

Three ways a caller ends up with no tenant claim, and they are three different
sentences. `tenantClaimGuard` tells them apart by whether a resolver ran at all.

| Situation | Status | Whose problem |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Nothing in this app emits the claim | 403 | the developer's — no resolver is configured |
| The request named no tenant | 403 | the caller's — the request is incomplete |
| The request named one they do not belong to | 403 | the caller's — refused |

**403 in every branch, and 401 in none.** 401 means *you have not proved who you
are*, and the caller has — every client treats it as a dead token, so a member of
A following a link into B was not refused, they were signed out of A (`FJS-383`).

## Per-tenant configuration

The allow-list of configuration keys a tenant may override.

**None. This app installs no `createApp({ tenantConfig })`**, so everything it is
configured with resolves once at boot and is the same for every tenant: the mail
transport and its from-address, a bucket, a timezone, a locale, a branding value,
a rate limit.

That is a legitimate app. What it cannot do is be one deployment that several
customers each experience as theirs, where the customer-facing half of *theirs* is
mostly not rows.
